root_cause: _attack_mode_monitor queries SQLite 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notifications WHERE timestamp > ?' but NO notifications table is ever created (grep CREATE TABLE.*notifications returns 0 matches). Notifications are stored in-memory (runtime/notifications.py:95 self._recent) + JSONL file (line 94). Query raises sqlite3.OperationalError, swallowed by except Exception: logger.debug(...). kill_count stays 0 → attack mode NEVER auto-triggers.
suggested_fix: Query the in-memory UserNotificationSystem singleton via judge.notifications._recent instead of SQLite. Replace SQL with: _notif = getattr(get_judge(), 'notifications', None); kill_count = sum(1 for n in _notif._recent if n.get('timestamp',0) > _time.time()-600 and n.get('event_type') in ('governance_kill','attack_blocked')) if _notif else 0. Remove duplicate dead code in api/_lifespan.py:285.
repro_hypothesis: Start SCP, send 50 attack prompts that get KILL verdicts. Check eng.in_attack_mode after 6min. It will be False. Debug logs show 'no such table: notifications' repeating.
why_R7_missed: R7 audited _lifespan task GC (R7-2) + crawler restart (R7-7) but never traced data flow inside _attack_mode_monitor. SQL string looks plausible; except swallows error silently (debug-level log). R7 grep scanner looked for except:pass patterns, not query-against-nonexistent-table patterns.

root_cause: _should_auto_approve_tier3 uses _tier3_auto_enabled_at == 0.0 as 'disabled' sentinel. On timeout expiry, line 1098 sets it to 0.0. But on the NEXT bug call, line 1091 sees == 0.0 and immediately re-arms by setting _tier3_auto_enabled_at = now (line 1092). The 1h timeout is ineffective — Tier-3 auto-approve stays permanently enabled as long as SCP_AUTO_APPROVE_TIER3=1 remains set, clock restarting on every bug after expiry. Comment at line 1095-1097 says 're-enable by setting SCP_AUTO_APPROVE_TIER3=1 again' but you don't need to.
suggested_fix: Add _tier3_auto_expired flag that does NOT clear on subsequent calls. Set _tier3_auto_expired=True on timeout. Clear only when env var transitions from 0/unset → 1 (track via _tier3_env_last_seen field). On next call: if _tier3_auto_enabled_at == 0.0 and _tier3_auto_expired: return False (don't re-arm).
world_tool: manual review + ruff PLR (logic) + semgrep python.lang.security.audit.timeout-bypass
repro_hypothesis: Set SCP_AUTO_APPROVE_TIER3=1. Wait 1h + 1 bug. Then send 5 more bugs over next hour. ALL 5 will still be auto-approved (timeout re-arms). WARNING fires once per expiry but doesn't actually disable.
why_R7_missed: R7-13 added audit log columns + rollback endpoint but never tested timeout behavior end-to-end. Logic looks correct in isolation (elif sets to 0.0 + returns False), but re-arm-on-next-call behavior invisible unless you trace SECOND call after expiry.

root_cause: _rotate_large_files docstring says 'Rotation: rename to .1.gz, shift existing .1.gz to .2.gz, delete .3.gz' implying 3 generations kept. Implementation does NOT shift — gzip.open(gz_path, 'wb') opens in write+truncate mode, OVERWRITING any existing .1.gz from previous rotation. After 2nd rotation, 1st rotation's compressed data is GONE. Only most recent rotation ever kept.
before_code:
gz_path = f.with_suffix(f.suffix + '.1.gz')
with open(f, 'rb') as src, gzip.open(gz_path, 'wb') as dst:
    shutil.copyfileobj(src, dst)
# (no shift of existing .1.gz to .2.gz, no deletion of .3.gz)
suggested_fix: Shift generations before writing new .1.gz: gz3.unlink() if exists; gz2.rename(gz3) if exists; gz1.rename(gz2) if exists; then write new gz1. Update docstring to match (or keep docstring as spec + fix code).
world_tool: vulture (dead code) + manual review + ruff DOC (docstring vs impl)
repro_hypothesis: Set ROTATE_SIZE_MB=0.1 for testing. Write 200MB to error_store.jsonl. Trigger rotation → .1.gz created. Write another 200MB. Trigger rotation → .1.gz OVERWRITTEN with 2nd batch. 1st batch's compressed data LOST.
why_R7_missed: R7-9 verified disk prune in canary_monitor.py but storage_manager.py's rotation was not in R7 audit scope. Docstring lies convincingly — readers assume shift happens.

root_cause: R7-7 added 12h stale WARN to detect stale knowledge base. Guard 'if last_success > 0 and (now - last_success) > 12*3600:' was intended to skip WARN before first successful crawl (avoid startup noise). But it ALSO skips WARN when first crawl NEVER succeeds. If SCP starts with network down, last_success stays 0.0 forever → 12h stale WARN NEVER fires. Operator gets zero signal that knowledge base is stale from cold start — exactly the failure R7-7 was supposed to catch.
before_code:
last_success = 0.0  #  tracks staleness for 12h healthcheck
...
#  12h healthcheck — WARN if no successful crawl in 12h.
if last_success > 0 and (now - last_success) > 12 * 3600:
    logger.warning(f' V100 crawler STALE — no successful crawl in {(now - last_success) / 3600:.1f}h...')
suggested_fix: Track _scheduler_started_at = time.time() at scheduler start. Fire WARN if 12h elapsed since start WITHOUT successful crawl: _stale_since = last_success if last_success > 0 else _scheduler_started_at; if now - _stale_since > 12*3600: logger.warning(...). Include cold_start={last_success==0} in message.
repro_hypothesis: Start SCP with no network. Wait 12h. Check logs — NO 'V100 crawler STALE' WARN fires (gated by last_success > 0 which is False for cold start). Crawler backoff ERROR logs fire, but 12h stale signal for operators missing.
why_R7_missed: R7-7 was about failure path (don't advance last_crawl on failure). Healthcheck guard 'last_success > 0' was 'skip startup noise' optimization, but cold-start interaction not tested. R7 hypothesis tests (R7-10) tested None-safety, not 12h WARN path.

root_cause: R7-13 Tier-3 auto-approve writes single .tier3bak per file: bak_path = filepath.with_suffix(filepath.suffix + '.tier3bak'); bak_path.write_text(...). This OVERWRITES any existing .tier3bak on same file. If bug A fixed (writes .tier3bak = pre-A), then bug B fixed on same file (writes .tier3bak = pre-B = post-A — OVERWRITES), .tier3bak for bug A is LOST. When operator POSTs /v105/autofix/rollback/{token_A}, endpoint reads .tier3bak (now pre-B state), computes hash, compares to before_hash (pre-A hash) — MISMATCH → HTTP 409 'Backup hash mismatch (backup tampered?)' — MISLEADING error suggesting tampering when real cause is backup clobbered by later fix on same file.
before_code:
# engine.py:1171 — single .tier3bak per file (OVERWRITES on 2nd fix same file)
bak_path = filepath.with_suffix(filepath.suffix + '.tier3bak')
bak_path.write_text(filepath.read_text(encoding='utf-8'), encoding='utf-8')

# v105_routes.py:340 — hash check fails for older fix on multi-fix file
bak_hash = _hashlib.sha256(bak_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
if bak_hash != before_hash:
    raise HTTPException(409, f'Backup hash mismatch (backup tampered?): expected={before_hash} got={bak_hash}')
suggested_fix: Per-token backup files: bak_path = filepath.with_suffix(filepath.suffix + f'.tier3bak.{_rollback_token}'). Update v105_routes.py:336 to derive bak_path from rollback_token. Update misleading 409 message to: 'Backup for token {token} missing or overwritten by a later fix on same file.'
world_tool: manual review + CodeQL data-flow (token → file → bak → hash)
repro_hypothesis: 1. SCP auto-approves bug A at foo.py:10 (writes foo.py.tier3bak = pre-A, audit token_A with before_hash=hash(pre-A)). 2. SCP auto-approves bug B at foo.py:20 (writes foo.py.tier3bak = pre-B — OVERWRITES). 3. Operator POSTs /v105/autofix/rollback/{token_A} → reads foo.py.tier3bak (now pre-B), hash != before_hash (pre-A) → HTTP 409 'tampered'. Error message LIES — backup wasn't tampered, it was clobbered by bug B.
why_R7_missed: R7-13 tested rollback with SINGLE fix per file (T2/T3/T4 in route docstring). Multi-fix-per-file case not tested. R7 reality test only verified 'rollback reverts file to before_hash' for single-fix file — hash check trivially passes when only one fix exists.

root_cause: V14SelfHealingEngine.heal() called from V98 pipeline thread (sync, inside judge.judge()). get_stats() called from API request thread (asyncio event loop). healing_history list mutated WITHOUT lock: heal() does self.healing_history.append({...}) + if len > 1000: self.healing_history = self.healing_history[-500:]. get_stats() does sum(1 for h in self.healing_history if h['success']). CPython list iterator caches ob_size; if heal() appends mid-iteration, next(iterator) raises RuntimeError: list changed size during iteration. asyncio event loop propagates as 500 error to admin client.
before_code:
# heal() line 213-218:
self.healing_history.append({'timestamp': ..., 'error_type': ..., 'strategy': strategy_name, 'success': success, 'duration': duration})
if len(self.healing_history) > 1000:
    self.healing_history = self.healing_history[-500:]

# get_stats() line 344-346:
total = len(self.healing_history)
successes = sum(1 for h in self.healing_history if h['success'])
avg_duration = sum(h['duration'] for h in self.healing_history) / max(1, total)
suggested_fix: Guard healing_history with threading.Lock: __init__ adds self._history_lock = threading.Lock(). heal() wraps append+truncate in 'with self._history_lock:'. get_stats() wraps iteration in 'with self._history_lock:'. Alternatively use collections.deque(maxlen=1000) to eliminate manual truncation race.
world_tool: manual review + semgrep python.lang.security.audit.race-condition + ruff RUF006
repro_hypothesis: Run SCP under load (concurrent /ask requests triggering heal() + admin polling /v98/status calling get_stats()). Eventually RuntimeError: list changed size during iteration appears in API response (500) or logs.
why_R7_missed: R7-3 added threading.Lock to why_engine.py for similar concurrent-claim race, but healing_v14.py not in R7 audit scope. Mutation pattern looks safe in isolation (single-threaded read), but cross-thread interaction invisible without tracing call sites.

root_cause: R7-3 added per-instance threading.Lock to serialize execute_pending_plans across in-process concurrent callers. Lazy-init pattern: 'if not hasattr(self, _execute_pending_lock): self._execute_pending_lock = _threading.Lock()'. Classic check-then-act race: if 2 threads enter concurrently and BOTH see not hasattr True (before either assigns), both create NEW Lock objects. Thread A assigns Lock_A; Thread B assigns Lock_B (overwrites Lock_A). If Thread B reaches 'with self._execute_pending_lock:' BEFORE Thread A overwrites attribute, Thread B acquires Lock_B. Then Thread A overwrites with Lock_A and acquires Lock_A. Both threads hold DIFFERENT locks → no mutual exclusion — exactly the race R7-3 was supposed to prevent. Window is tiny (few bytecodes between hasattr and with) but real — CPython GIL releases between bytecodes.
before_code:
import threading as _threading
# [R7-3+] Per-instance lock — guards in-process concurrency.
if not hasattr(self, '_execute_pending_lock'):
    self._execute_pending_lock = _threading.Lock()
...
with self._execute_pending_lock:
    try:
        #  Atomic claim: UPDATE returns only rows THIS thread claimed.
suggested_fix: Initialize lock in __init__ (eager init), not lazily: def __init__(self, ...): ...; self._execute_pending_lock = threading.Lock(). def execute_pending_plans(self, ...): with self._execute_pending_lock: ... (no lazy init — lock always exists). Or use class-level lock to guard instance lock creation. Eager init is simpler + race-free.
repro_hypothesis: Hammer execute_pending_plans with 10 concurrent threads from stress test (10 simultaneous /admin/why/execute calls). With enough iterations, 2 threads will both create separate Lock objects and both proceed to claim same why_verification_plans row. DB-level claimed_by column catches this (R7-3 defense-in-depth), so no data corruption — but in-process lock's purpose (avoiding wasted DB contention) is defeated.
why_R7_missed: R7-3's fix tested for common case (sequential calls). Race window tiny; stress-testing concurrent execute_pending_plans calls not in R7 hypothesis tests (R7-10 tested None-safety, not concurrency stress). hasattr lazy-init pattern is common Python idiom that LOOKS safe but has this subtle race.
